purpose: Test whether smaller llama.cpp batching and one server slot make a long CRAFT prompt tractable on the available 8 GB GPU. Not a language comparison.
question: With one inference slot and smaller prompt batches, can the pinned Qwen3-8B CRAFT runner complete two turns, deliver the three distinct Director messages, and make nonzero progress?

adapter: Sample D1, D2, D3 without replacement and seed the Python scheduler.
Preserve non-instruction bracketed Director prose in the parser fallback.
Set child process console encoding to UTF-8.

model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; 99 GPU layers; 8192 context; 1 parallel slot; logical batch 512; physical micro-batch 128; reasoning off; Director temperature 0.7/max_tokens 500; Builder temperature 0.1/max_tokens 250

design.communication_condition: upstream CRAFT natural-language prompts and messages with bracket-preserving parser fallback
design.status_relative_to_v0_19: same structure/model/task, fresh scheduling seed, different server memory settings; separate run

primary: whether each requested completion finishes, with wall time
per turn: generated Director posts, parsed messages, and Builder-delivered messages, reported separately
upstream overall_progress after each completed turn
secondary: GPU memory/utilization snapshots at request stalls, if any

predictions: At least one Director completion will finish within ten minutes of request start.
If two turns complete, each will deliver at least two of the three Director messages.
analysis: If the first request again stalls for five continuous minutes with no increase in prompt-processed or decoded-token counts, stop before issuing further calls and report a runtime failure. Otherwise complete the fixed two-turn budget. Report all partial and complete attempts.
